fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Many people grind or clench their teeth without realising it, often while they sleep or during periods of concentration or stress. Over time, this habit can wear teeth down, cause cracks and lead to jaw pain, headaches and sensitivity.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we look for the signs of grinding and clenching during your examination and can recommend ways to protect your teeth.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Grinding and Clenching?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Grinding and clenching are known as bruxism. Grinding involves moving the teeth against one another, while clenching involves pressing the teeth firmly together. Both place considerable force on the teeth, jaw joints and muscles.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Bruxism can occur during sleep or while awake. It is associated with factors such as stress, anxiety, sleep disorders including sleep apnoea, certain medications, caffeine, alcohol and smoking.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Is Treatment Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You may benefit from an assessment if you notice:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Flattened, worn or chipped teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Tooth sensitivity or cracked teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Aching jaw muscles, particularly on waking

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Morning headaches or tension around the temples

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Clicking or discomfort in the jaw joint

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A partner mentioning grinding noises at night

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Scalloped edges on your tongue or marks inside your cheeks

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If you have crowns, veneers or implants, protecting them from grinding forces is especially important.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Assessment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We ask about your symptoms, sleep and lifestyle, and examine your teeth for wear, cracks and fractures. We also check your jaw joints and muscles and assess your bite.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Discussion of Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We explain what we find and discuss the most suitable approach. For many people, a custom night splint is recommended to protect the teeth. Where sleep apnoea is suspected, we may suggest you speak with your GP about further assessment.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Custom Splint Fabrication

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Using our 3D intra-oral scanner or impressions, we record your teeth accurately. Your splint is then made to fit your bite closely.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Fitting

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We check the fit and comfort of your splint, adjust your bite on the appliance and show you how to wear and care for it.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Repairing Damage

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If grinding has already caused damage, restorations such as fillings, dental crowns or porcelain veneers may be discussed, along with measures to protect them.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Wear your splint as directed, usually at night. Clean it each morning with a soft brush and cool water, and store it in its case. Bring it to your check-ups so we can assess its fit and wear. Strategies such as reducing caffeine and alcohol in the evening, relaxation techniques and being mindful of daytime clenching may also help. Jaw exercises or physiotherapy may be suggested in some cases.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Grinding and Clenching

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Grinding and Clenching

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We take a thorough, whole-picture approach, looking at your teeth, jaw, bite and lifestyle. With digital scanning, we can create accurate, comfortable splints, and we monitor your teeth over time as part of your preventive care for adults.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How do I know if I grind my teeth at night?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Common signs include jaw aches or headaches on waking, worn or chipped teeth, and a partner noticing grinding sounds. We can look for signs at your check-up.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will a night splint stop me grinding?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A splint does not always stop grinding, but it helps protect your teeth from wear and reduce pressure on your jaw joints and muscles.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I use a store-bought guard?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Over-the-counter guards may not fit closely and can sometimes affect the bite. A custom splint is designed specifically for your teeth.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can grinding crack my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Repeated grinding and clenching forces can lead to chips and cracks. In some cases, a broken tooth may need restorative treatment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is grinding linked to stress?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Stress and anxiety are common contributing factors, along with sleep disorders, caffeine, alcohol and some medications.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Are night splints covered by health funds?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many extras policies with dental cover provide rebates for occlusal splints. We can provide item numbers to help you check.
